senses.definition: A photograph, especially one taken quickly or in a sudden moment of opportunity.
examples: He carried a snapshot of his daughter.

senses.definition: A glimpse of something; a portrayal of something at a moment in time.
examples: The article offered a snapshot of life in that region.

quotes.text: I hope you've enjoyed reading this series. As usual, it's just a snapshot because there's so much to say but only so many words can make it into print.
quotes.reference: 2020 December 2, Paul Bigland, “My weirdest and wackiest Rover yet”, in Rail, page 70:

senses.definition: (computing) A file or set of files captured at a particular time, often capable of being reloaded to restore the earlier state.
examples: This game is so hard that I find myself taking a snapshot every few seconds in case I get killed.

senses.definition: (soccer) A quick, unplanned or unexpected shot.

quotes.text: Yet Revell misjudged his promising position in the area to put his point-blank snapshot wide from only six yards out.
quotes.reference: 2011 March 2, Chris Whyatt, “Arsenal 5 - 0 Leyton Orient”, in BBC:

senses.definition: (firearms) A quick offhand shot, made without deliberately taking aim over the sights.

quotes.text: How quick the eye and hand to catch him [the ruffed grouse] when he rises from the underbrush and is out of sight in the wood before the untrained sportsman stops him with what is little more than a snapshot, so instantaneously must all be done!
quotes.reference: 1892, Stanley Waterloo, A Man and a Woman:

quotes.text: As he did not appear disposed to move off, I took my camera and approached within about thirty yards, when I snapshotted him.
quotes.reference: 1904, David T Hanbury, Sport and Travel in the Northland of Canada:

senses.definition: (transitive, computing) To capture the state of, in a snapshot.

quotes.text: Filer appliances also offer programmatic snapshotting and cloning at the block-level or file system-level.
